title: CJP holds Tricolour march at Azad Maidan in Mumbai

tea.why: Protesting the arrest of party leaders in Delhi after an incident at Jantar Mantar.
tea.want: To show solidarity with arrested activists and assert that displaying the national flag is not a crime.
tea.changed: Oct 16: CJP supporters gathered at Azad Maidan in Mumbai to hold a tricolour march.

summary: The Cockroach Janata Party organized a one-day Tricolour march at Azad Maidan in Mumbai to express solidarity with arrested party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das. The leaders were previously detained and remanded to judicial custody by Delhi Police following an incident at Jantar Mantar where members allegedly entered the denotified protest site without permission to unfurl the national flag. Mumbai Police granted official permission for the Azad Maidan demonstration as it is a designated protest site. Supporters gathered to voice their dissent and demand recognition that displaying the national flag should not be considered a crime, while similar demonstrations were proposed in New Delhi.
demands: Affirm that waving the national flag is not a crime
response: Mumbai Police granted permission for the one-day march at Azad Maidan, noting it is a designated protest site.

updates.text: Mumbai Police confirmed permission was granted to the CJP for a one-day Tricolour march at Azad Maidan on October 16.
CJP supporters gathered at Mumbai's Azad Maidan to hold the planned tricolour march in solidarity with arrested activists.
